messages:
alex_support: FYI — Acme (tenant acme-42) opened an escalation: sudden p99 jump on /generate since ~2026-02-12T10:30Z. p95 ~1.1s -> 2.4s, p99 ~0.8s -> 6.2s. Customer very impacted.

dana_oncall: Can you paste the error snippets and the model + node where it's happening? Any OOM logs?

alex_support: Paste from runtime logs: 
```
OOM: allocation of 134217728 bytes failed at allocator.cc:482
slab_eviction: loop_count=32 tenant=acme-42
WARN: kv_insert_failed: tenant=acme-42 key_count=2712341
```
Also seeing repeated auth retries around the same time (500s -> 429s on retry).

priya_eng: Pulling metrics now. Early look: tenant heat on node gpu-123. Last hour snapshots: 
- runtime_kv_entries{tenant="acme-42"} = 2.7e6
- gpu_mem_total_bytes = 25769803776
- gpu_mem_allocated_bytes = 233203... (≈21.7GB)
- gpu_mem_free_bytes ≈ 2.3GB
- slab_frag_ratio = 0.62
This smells like KV growth + fragmentation (allocator can't satisfy big contiguous blocks -> slow path + evictions).

jon_support: Customer also notes their requests occasionally return 502 + long connection times during the window. They saw auth retries when the backend timed out.

dana_oncall: Ok — immediate ask: can we reproduce in staging? Priya, do we have a replay harness for Acme traffic shape (long contexts w/ lots of distinct prefixes)?

priya_eng: Yes. Repro steps I used locally (staging):
```
# replay script (staging)
for i in $(seq 1 5000); do
  curl -s -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $STAGING_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-22-large","input":"user:'$RANDOM' long-prompts ...","max_tokens":256}' &
done
```
Warmup with many unique prefixes to grow KV entries. In staging this pushed slab_frag_ratio > 0.6 and we saw p99 spikes.

ops-bot: [alert] node=gpu-123 slab_eviction_rate=0.63, kv_entries_delta=+420k/15m, p99_latency_route=/generate=6.1s

dana_oncall: Quick mitigations to buy time for the customer: 
1) Move tenant to a smaller model variant (gpt-22-medium) or to a different node with more free GPU RAM.
2) Temporarily disable prefix caching / per-tenant KV caching for acme-42 (stop growth).
3) Increase slab_compact frequency on the node (aggressive compaction).
4) If needed, enable fallback routing to dedicated CPU-backed variant to avoid backend stalls.
I can apply 1+2 now if Alex approves.

alex_support: doing 1 & 2 now — route override to redwood/gpt-22-medium and set tenant_kv_ttl=30m to cap growth. Command I used:
```
# route override
redwoodctl routes set --tenant acme-42 --model redwood/gpt-22-medium --note "temp: alloc-shock mitigation"
# disable tenant prefix caching
redwoodctl tenant-config patch acme-42 --set caching.prefix=false --set kv.ttl=1800
```

priya_eng: Good. Also two medium-term fixes we should consider: 
- Expose per-tenant KV cap with graceful evict (hard cap + tail-drop).
- Tweak allocator tunables: reduce max slab size from 64MB -> 32MB for fragmentation-heavy nodes, increase slab_compact throttle to run every 30s when frag>0.55.
Config snippet for test patch:
```
allocator.tunables {
  slab_max_size_mb = 32
  slab_compact_interval_s = 30
  eviction_aggressiveness = 1.5
}
```
These reduced p99 in staging repro by ~75% in our local runs.

dana_oncall: Can we also add an alert for slab_frag_ratio > 0.55 per-node and for kv_entries growth rate > 200k/15m? That would get us ahead.

priya_eng: Yep — I will add those alerts and open RN-3245 to track allocator diffs + per-tenant KV cap work.

ops-bot: [action] route override applied for acme-42 -> redwood/gpt-22-medium by alex_support at 2026-02-12T10:46Z

alex_support: Update from customer: p99 dropped to ~900ms within 8 minutes after the route override and TTL. They still see occasional slow tails but much improved. :thumbsup:

lauren_acme: On behalf of Acme: confirmed — latency is back to acceptable levels. Thanks for the quick patch. Please follow up with root cause & a timeline for a permanent fix.

jon_support: Noted, I'll send the customer a brief summary and ETA for next steps.

priya_eng: Follow-ups for eng: 
- Open ticket RN-3245 (allocator experiments + per-tenant KV cap), assign to runtime infra.
- Add playbook steps to runbook 'alloc-frag-mitigation' (include move-to-smaller-model, disable-caching, route-override commands).
- Postmortem if we see recurrence within 7 days.

dana_oncall: Agree. I'll create the incident doc and schedule a quick retro with runtime + support tomorrow. Thanks everyone.

alex_support: Closing customer-facing loop now. Will attach logs + repro steps to RN-3245.

priya_eng: ack, will start the allocator test branch today.

lauren_acme: Thanks again. Appreciate the fast response.

(ends)
